facts.title: Unrefusable Financial Offer for Reunion (2023)
facts.body: By 2023, the financial offer for an Oasis reunion had escalated to an unprecedented amount that was "impossible to refuse," regardless of other considerations. This significant financial incentive became a key driver for the brothers' agreement to reunite. "But sometime in 2023, the offer had grown to a point where no one could refuse for any reason."

facts.title: Keith Richards' 2023 View on Modern Music
facts.body: In 2023, Keith Richards expressed strong disapproval of modern music production techniques, citing the use of "push button drums" and synthesized sounds. He described digital recording as a "one-way toilet," indicating his preference for older, more organic methods of music creation. This sentiment from Richards, who played guitar for Mick Jagger on the song "Man, What a Drag It Is Getting Old," highlights a generational perspective on musical change. "Don't get me going on modern day music, push button drums and everything is synthesized. Digital recording is a one-way toilet."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: What A Drag It Is Getting Old (Musically)
facts.name: The Rolling Stones

facts.title: Death (July 26, 2023) – Found Unresponsive in London Apartment; Coroner Ruled Natural Causes in January 2024
facts.body: Sinéad O'Connor led a troubled life with both physical and mental health struggles from the beginning. During her career she became an icon for refusing to bend to anyone or anything, always doing everything her own way. She survived multiple suicide attempts over the years, and friends and followers were regularly concerned about her well-being. She was found unresponsive in her London apartment on July 26, 2023, and was declared dead at the scene. In January 2024, the Coroner's report determined she died of natural causes — nothing suspicious, case closed. Her first two albums are considered stone-cold classics. "She became an icon as someone who refused to bend and insisted on doing everything and I mean everything her way."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Sinead O'Connor

facts.title: Incomplete Memoir and Final Projects (2023)
facts.body: Sinead O'Connor authored an "excellent yet incomplete" memoir titled *Remembrings*, which sold very well. At the time of her death, she had an album of new material "almost finished" and was planning tour dates for 2024 and 2025. "She wrote an excellent yet incomplete memoir called Remembrings That Sold Very Well."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Sinead O'Connor

facts.title: Death (July 26, 2023)
facts.body: Sinead O'Connor passed away on July 26, 2023, at approximately 11:20 AM, found unresponsive in her flat on the south side of London. Police pronounced her dead at the scene, and her death was not considered suspicious. She was 56 years old. "But at about 1120 in the morning of July 26, 2023, police were called to her flat. She was found unresponsive and pronounced dead at the scene."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Sinead O'Connor

facts.title: Death at 56 (2023)
facts.body: Sinéad O'Connor was found dead in her London flat on July 26th, 2023, at the age of 56. After months of investigation, her cause of death was determined to be natural causes, specifically Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) from years of smoking, exacerbated by asthma and a low-grade respiratory infection. Her passing garnered worldwide news coverage, and her memorial was attended by thousands, including Bono and the President of Ireland. "But on July 26th, she was found dead in her flat. She was only 56."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 3: (80-71)
facts.name: Sinead O'Connor

facts.title: 2023 Album Project
facts.body: In early 2023, before her death, Sinéad O'Connor had moved to London and was actively working on what was anticipated to be a new album. "In early 2023, she was working on what was going to be another album, and she moved to London."

facts.title: Andy Rourke Death (May 18, 2023) – Pancreatic Cancer, Age 59; Sued Morrissey, Later Played Two Morrissey Singles
facts.body: Andy Rourke was a founding member of the Smiths and is considered by fans one of the greatest bassists in the history of British indie rock. His time with the band ended badly: a heroin addiction, a lawsuit against Morrissey and Johnny Marr for unpaid royalties (he was broke), and a decade later a bankruptcy over tax issues. Post-Smiths, he worked with the Pretenders, Killing Joke, Stone Roses singer Ian Brown, Dolores O'Riordan and the Cranberries, and Peter Hook of New Order. In a remarkable reconciliation, he played on two Morrissey solo singles despite the money disputes. His father and sister were both diagnosed with cancer, which prompted him to start a cancer charity; he himself was later diagnosed with pancreatic cancer. He died in a New York hospital on May 18, 2023, age 59. "Ask any Smiths fan, and they'll tell you that he was one of the greatest bassists in the history of British Indie Rock."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: The Smiths

facts.title: Coachella Comeback Performance (2023)

facts.title: Steve Mackey Death (March 2, 2023) – Undisclosed Illness, Age 56; Produced Florence and the Machine's Lungs; Appeared in Harry Potter
facts.body: Steve Mackey joined Pulp in 1989 and was their bassist through the glory years of the 1990s Britpop era before leaving around 2002. He became a producer and remix artist, working with Cornershop, The Kills, and The Horrors, and co-produced Florence and the Machine's debut album *Lungs*. He also worked as a music director and sound designer for institutions including the Louvre, the Museum of Modern Art, and a Shanghai museum. Harry Potter fans may know him as one of the Weird Sisters in *Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire* — a group that also featured Jarvis Cocker of Pulp and Johnny Greenwood and Phil Selway of Radiohead. When Pulp announced a reunion in early 2023, Mackey did not want to participate — in retrospect, probably because he was already ill. His death was announced March 2, 2023, having been in hospital since Christmas 2022 with an undisclosed condition. He was 56. "In retrospect, that's probably because he was ill."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Pulp

facts.title: Tom Verlaine Death (January 28, 2023) – Prostate Cancer, Age 73; Helped CBGB Become Ground Zero for Punk
facts.body: Tom Verlaine co-founded Television and in 1973 helped Hilly Kristal — owner of a scuzzy bar on Bleecker Street in a then-terrible part of New York — to let Television play a Sunday night residency. This decision catalyzed CBGB into becoming ground zero for New York punk and, by chain reaction, the entire international punk movement. Television produced two critically acclaimed albums before breaking up in 1978. Verlaine subsequently collaborated with Patti Smith, worked with James Iha of the Smashing Pumpkins, had a song covered by David Bowie, and was involved in a 1992 Television reunion album. He was scheduled to produce Jeff Buckley's second album — a project ended when Buckley drowned in the Mississippi River in 1997. Verlaine was diagnosed with prostate cancer at some point in the 2000s; it metastasized. He died January 28, 2023, age 73. "That was the catalyst for making CBGB ground zero for the world of New York punk."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Television

facts.title: Jim Gordon Death (March 13, 2023) – Died of Natural Causes in Psychiatric Prison at 77; Killed Mother in 1983
facts.body: Jim Gordon was a highly respected session drummer in the 1960s who played on dozens of recordings and performed with Eric Clapton in Derek and the Dominoes, including on the classic "Layla." He then developed severe schizophrenia — voices told him to starve himself, he couldn't sleep, was alcoholic, and received the wrong treatment. On June 3, 1983, a voice told him to attack his mother with a hammer and stab her to death with a butcher knife. He did. He was sentenced to prison and denied parole at least 10 times due to the severity of his mental illness; he remained in a psychiatric facility until he died of natural causes on March 13, 2023, at age 77. "A voice told him to attack his mother with a hammer and stab her to death with a butcher knife. So he did."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: Alan Rankine Death (January 2, 2023) – Heart Disease, Age 64; Launched Snow Patrol, Belle & Sebastian, Biffy Clyro via Electric Honey Records
facts.body: Alan Rankine co-founded the Associates with Billy MacKenzie in Dundee, Scotland in 1979 — evolving out of post-punk bands and following a Bowie-like direction. A former competitive tennis player (too short at 5'8" to go professional), Rankine also worked as a production collaborator with the Cocteau Twins. After the Associates broke up, he became a lecturer at Stow College in Glasgow teaching music production, and helped students set up a record label called Electric Honey, which launched Snow Patrol, Belle & Sebastian, and Biffy Clyro. He was diagnosed with heart disease in the 2020s and died at home with family on January 2, 2023, at age 64. "He helped him set up a record label called Electric Honey, and that label launched the careers of bands like Snow Patrol, Bell and Sebastian, and Biffy Clyro."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: Vivian Trimble Death (April 4, 2023) – Cancer, Age 59; Bandmate Kate Schellenbach Was Briefly in Beastie Boys
facts.body: Vivian Trimble was keyboardist for Luscious Jackson, an early 1990s New York group mixing alt-rock, rap, and pop. Their connection to the Beastie Boys ran deep: drummer Kate Schellenbach had actually been an early Beastie Boys member before producer Rick Rubin had her ousted. Luscious Jackson toured with the Beasties and became the first signing to the Beastie Boys' Grand Royal record label. Their most successful album was *Fever In Fever Out* (1996, over 500,000 copies), featuring the alt-rock radio hit "Naked Eye." Vivian left in 1998 to settle down with a family, moved to New Hampshire, and worked as a music venue booker. She was diagnosed with cancer and died April 4, 2023, age 59. "Vivian left the group in 1998 because she was tired of touring."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: Steve Harwell Death (September 4, 2023) – Alcoholism, Son's Leukemia Death, Cardiomyopathy, Age 56
facts.body: Steve Harwell struggled with alcoholism for most of his adult life, a condition that worsened after his infant son Presley died at six months from leukemia. Alcohol destroyed his liver. In 2013 he was diagnosed with cardiomyopathy (heart muscle disease); by 2015 he had Wernicke encephalopathy from alcohol damage, causing balance problems, confusion, and vision impairment. By 2021, his health made continuing with Smash Mouth impossible. Following an erratic onstage performance at a New York festival, the band issued a statement confirming he was retiring to focus on his health. In August 2023, he began hospice care at his home in Boise, Idaho. He died September 4, 2023, age 56. "The truth was, nothing could be done for Steve."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Smash Mouth

facts.title: Blackie O'Nassis Death (June 13, 2023) – Drummer on Pulp Fiction's "Girl, You'll Be a Woman Soon"; Age 57, Cause Unknown
facts.body: John Rowan, who played under the name Blackie O'Nassis, was the drummer for Urge Overkill — the Chicago band whose cover of Neil Diamond's "Girl, You'll Be a Woman Soon" (1967) appears in the famous dance scene in *Pulp Fiction*. The band was also a cult favorite in the alt-rock community and opened for Nirvana on the *Nevermind* tour, during which they befriended Kurt Cobain, Chrissie Hynde of the Pretenders, and Liz Phair. Blackie left the band in 1996; there were reports of heroin use and at least one arrest. The cause of his death on June 13, 2023, at age 57 was never disclosed. "As for the cause of his death on June 13th, 2023, we have no idea."

facts.body: Released a month prior to the review, this album received generally very good critical reviews. It was described as more experimental and marked the first time Noel Gallagher did not produce himself, instead collaborating with David Holmes, a "very old school British electronic artist." The album successfully innovates Noel Gallagher's sound while still appealing to fans of his classic style, evolving his music without losing his loyal audience and attracting new listeners. It incorporates experimental elements not as electronic music itself, but through the use of noises, loops, and samples from various sources, such as a woman with scissors, a telephone ringing, or car sounds. These unexpected elements are integrated based on a solid understanding of his core sound. The album's structure begins with a long instrumental piece, filled with saturated sounds and noises, designed to prepare the listener for the blend of mixed influences and his classic sound. While the instrumental aspects and production are highly praised, the lyrics are noted as weaker and more "banal" compared to his previous work, suggesting a focus on sound over lyrical complexity. "ha conseguido evolucinar su sonido sin perder al público fil que tenía."
facts.source: Music Radar Clan

facts.title: Hamas Terrorist Attack (2023)
facts.body: On October 7, 2023, the Supernova Festival, an EDM event in Southern Israel coordinated for Jewish holidays and promoted as a celebration of "friends, love, and infinite freedom," came under attack by Hamas fighters. Just after sunrise, as part of a larger push into Israel, Hamas fighters on foot, motorcycles, trucks, and powered paragliders, armed with AK-47s, assault rifles, hand grenades, and rocket-propelled grenades, surrounded the festival grounds. They opened fire on attendees, executing many who tried to escape. The attack killed at least 364 people, including 17 police officers, injured hundreds, and resulted in 40 or more festival-goers being taken hostage to the Gaza Strip, along with numerous reports of sexual assaults. "It was the largest terror attack in the history of Israel, and the worst massacre of Israeli citizens ever. It was the worst killing of Jews since the Holocaust."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: Ghostwriter's "Heart on My Sleeve" (2023)
facts.body: In April 2023, an individual known as Ghostwriter created and released a fake duet titled "Heart on My Sleeve," featuring AI-generated voices that mimicked Drake and The Weeknd. This two-minute track immediately drew intense public attention and sparked widespread debates concerning the ethical and legal ramifications of using artists' voices without their consent. "The one that got everybody's attention was a fake duet between a fake Drake and a fake the weekend created and posted in April 2023 by someone named Ghost Rider."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: Artist Adoption of AI for Songwriting (April & July 2023 Surveys)
facts.body: Surveys in April and July 2023 showed significant artist adoption of AI tools. An April survey of 1,300 artists found over 60% used AI for songwriting (11% for creation, 20% for production, 31% for mastering). A July survey of 1,600 artists revealed half viewed AI positively, and a third planned to use it for new tunes or marketing/promotion. "In April 2023 a survey of 1,300 artists revealed that over 60% of them were already using AI as some kind of songwriting tool."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: Record Store Day 2023 Trend: Live Albums
facts.body: Unlike last year's focus on 7-inch singles, this year's Record Store Day sees a notable trend towards live albums. Artists are widely choosing to release either unreleased, re-edited, or famous bootleg live albums, aiming to engage their fanbases. "este año destacan, los álbumes en directo, este año todo el mundo ha optado por lanzar álbumes en directo, inéditos o reditados o bootlegs famosos, un poco para enganchar los fans."

facts.body: John Hinckley Jr., who attempted to assassinate President Ronald Reagan, was released unconditionally in 2022 and has since pursued a music career, releasing a debut album in July 2023. "Was released unconditionally in 2022 and now makes music, having released a debut album in July 2023."

facts.title: Notable Deaths of 2023 – A Partial List
facts.body: Among the significant musicians lost in 2023: Jeff Beck (January 10, bacterial meningitis, age 78 — regarded by some as the greatest electric guitarist of all time); Tina Turner (May 24, kidney disease, cardiovascular problems, and intestinal cancer, age 83); Randy Meisner of the Eagles (July 25, COPD, age 77 — his wife had accidentally shot herself in 2016); Gary Wright (August 30, Parkinson's and Lewy Body dementia, age 80 — "Dreamweaver," 1976); Burt Bacharach (February 8, age 94); Gordon Lightfoot (May 1, age 84 — almost died of an aortic aneurysm in 2002 and a stroke in 2006 but fought back each time); Tony Bennett (July 21, age 96 — career began 1936); Jimmy Buffett (September 1, rare aggressive skin cancer, age 76); Shane MacGowan of The Pogues (November 30, pneumonia and encephalitis); Gordon Lightfoot; Sixto Rodriguez (August 8, age 81 — subject of the Oscar-winning documentary *Searching for Sugar Man*); David Crosby (January, COVID complications, age 81); Seymour Stein, founder of Sire Records and the man who signed Madonna, the Pretenders, the Smiths, and dozens of British acts to North American deals. "Every year this list gets longer and longer and longer."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: Blink 182 Surprise Headliner (2023)
facts.body: On April 14, 2023, Blink 182 was announced as a surprise replacement headliner for R&B singer Frank Ocean, who had to cancel with only two days' notice. This performance marked the first time the original lineup (Mark, Travis, Tom) had played together in nine years, drawing 150,000 attendees for an hour-long set that was described as "one big sing along." "And with just two days to go, Blink 182 was announced as his surprise replacement."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
